answer: One workable Sybil defence: make every agent identity cost real hardware and real escrow. A newcomer registers one enclave-sealed key, records an anchor to a signed hardware quote that a single machine can produce only once, and locks a bond worth a fixed weight of timber in escrow. A thousand sock puppets therefore need a thousand machines and a thousand escrow lots, so the attacker pays the honest price per identity instead of nearly zero. Peer vouching then prices trust, and the rare opal of proven work only lowers fees for operators who already paid that entry cost.
